purpose: Can the proper-divisor tile strips exactly match the target strip?
meaning: A positive integer is perfect when the sum of its positive proper divisors equals the integer itself. List the divisors smaller than n, make one counted strip for each divisor, and compare their combined length s with the target n. The balance Δ=s−n distinguishes deficient, perfect and abundant numbers.

definition.setting: A number exhibit has a target strip of n unit tiles. For every positive proper divisor d of n, it builds one separate strip with d tiles. Collect these divisor strips and compare their total with the target. The picture counts each proper divisor once; it does not partition the original strip into those pieces.
definition.formal_latex: D=\{d\in\mathbb{N}:d\mid n,\ 0<d<n\},\quad s=\sum_{d\in D}d,\quad \Delta=s-n,\quad n\text{ is perfect}\iff s=n.

properties.conditions: The target is a whole number from 1 to 60 items. A proper divisor is positive and strictly smaller than n. For n=1 the proper-divisor set is empty and its sum is zero.
properties.derivation: A positive divisor d of n leaves zero remainder in integer division. Excluding n leaves exactly the proper divisors. Add each member once and subtract n to obtain the balance. At n=1 there are no allowed members, so the empty sum is zero and the balance is −1. Divisor pairs found up to the square root give an independent check, counting a square-root divisor only once.
